dataset_info.name: VEDA AyurMind AI — Diseases & Therapeutic Herbs Dataset
dataset_info.part_description: Diseases DIS-061 to DIS-120 (G to P)
dataset_info.source_text: Dravyaguna Vijnana — Therapeutic Indication of Drugs & Technical Medical Terminology
dataset_info.description: Part 2 of 3 — Ayurvedic disease-herb mapping. Each entry includes disease ID, English name, Sanskrit name, category, description, herbs with botanical names, associated Sanskrit technical terms with meanings, and herb count.

diseases.description: Sexually transmitted bacterial infection causing purulent urethral or vaginal discharge, painful urination and pelvic inflammation. One of the 20 types of Prameha in Ayurveda.

Chronic intestinal disorder of the Grahani organ (seat of Agni) causing malabsorption, alternating constipation and diarrhoea, loss of appetite and undigested food in stool. Correlates with IBS, sprue and chronic amoebiasis.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disorders of Grahani organ; malabsorption syndrome; chronic amoebiasis/colitis

diseases.description: Accumulation forming a palpable lump in the abdomen from wind and other factors; phantom tumour or gas mass. Classified as Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Raktaja and Sannipataja types.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Abdominal lump caused by accumulation of wind and other causes
A lump formed in uterus due to accumulation of menstrual blood
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Internal bleeding due to vitiation of Rakta (blood) and Pitta; manifests as bleeding from nose, mouth, anus, urethra or vagina. A serious Pitta disorder requiring urgent treatment.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Intrinsic haemorrhage due to vitiation of rakta (blood) and pitta (bile)

diseases.description: Various disorders affecting the heart including coronary artery disease, cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias and heart failure. Hridroga is rooted in Tridosha imbalance affecting the Hridaya (heart organ — the seat of Ojas).
Protrusion of an organ or tissue through a weakened area in the abdominal wall; inguinal, umbilical or incisional hernia.
Involuntary spasmodic contraction of the diaphragm with sudden intake of breath and characteristic sound. Caused by upward movement of Vata (Udana Vata) in Ayurveda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Abnormal change in voice quality; rough, strained, weak or lost voice due to laryngeal conditions, Vata vitiation in vocal cord region or post-infectious changes.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Curing, cleaning and improving throat disorders; soothing to throat

diseases.description: Discomfort or pain in upper abdomen after eating; bloating, nausea, heaviness. Impaired processing of food due to weakened Jatharagni (gastric digestive fire).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Food intoxication associated with faulty digestion and impaired metabolism

diseases.description: The body's immune response to injury or infection causing redness, heat, pain and swelling. Corresponds to Shotha and Svayathu in Ayurveda; primarily a Pitta-Kapha or Vata-Pitta condition.
Mental disorder characterised by disturbed thinking, perception, behaviour and emotion. Classified as Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Sannipataja and Agantuja (exogenous) Unmada in Ayurveda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Inducing psychotropic effects; stimulating central nervous system

diseases.description: Persistent inability to fall or stay asleep; sleep disorder causing fatigue and reduced daytime function. Caused by Vata aggravation in the nervous system and mind (Manas).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Yellowing of skin, mucous membranes and whites of eyes due to elevated bilirubin; indicates liver dysfunction, bile duct obstruction or haemolysis. Includes hepatitis. Halimaka is the advanced severe stage.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Advanced stage or case of jaundice

diseases.description: Broad category of chronic skin diseases. Kshudrakushtha covers 11 minor skin diseases; Mahakushtha covers 7 major diseases including leprosy. In Ayurveda, all three Doshas plus Rakta, Twak, Mamsa and Lasika are involved.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Generally skin disease; particularly leprosy — Kshudrakushtha and Mahakushtha
A skin disease causing darkness, roughening and hardness of skin
Psoriasis; chronic skin inflammation with silvery scaled patches
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Abnormal enlargement of the liver (hepatomegaly); may indicate infection, fatty liver, cirrhosis or malignancy.
Excess body fat accumulation with BMI above normal; associated with metabolic syndrome, diabetes and cardiovascular risk. In Ayurveda, excess Kapha and Medo dhatu (fat tissue) accumulation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Aids in reducing corpulence; reduction of body weight

diseases.description: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in body tissues causing swelling; generalised (anasarca) or localised. Caused by Tridosha imbalance; classified as Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja and Sannipataja types.
Various diseases and conditions specific to children. Kaumarabhritya (Ayurvedic paediatrics) covers childhood diseases from birth to adolescence including Balagraha (childhood seizure syndromes).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Seizures in children causing various syndromes

diseases.description: Swollen veins in rectum or around anus causing pain, itching, bleeding and discomfort. Classified into Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja and Sannipataja; also wet (bleeding) and dry (non-bleeding) types.
Haemorrhoids with active bleeding; bright red blood in stools or on toilet paper after defecation. Pitta-dominant type requiring haemostatic treatment.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Intrinsic haemorrhage due to vitiation of blood and bile

diseases.description: Toxic effects from ingestion, inhalation or contact with harmful substances including plant, animal and mineral toxins. Ayurveda classifies as Sthavara (plant/mineral) and Jangama (animal) Visha.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Indicated and useful in countering spider-bite poisoning

diseases.description: Fatal viral encephalitis transmitted through the bite of infected animals; causes progressive neurological symptoms, agitation, hydrophobia and death if untreated.
Envenomation from snake bite causing local tissue destruction, haemotoxicity or neurotoxicity depending on species. Requires immediate antidotal treatment.
Envenomation from scorpion sting; causes local intense pain, numbness and potential systemic toxicity including cardiac and neurological effects.
Toxic effects from spider bite; causes local necrosis or systemic effects depending on spider species.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Indicated and useful in countering spider-bite poisoning

diseases.description: Toxic effects from rat bite or rat-borne toxins; historically referenced in classical Ayurvedic toxicology texts.
Viral infections causing characteristic skin eruptions with pox lesions; includes variola (smallpox) and varicella (chickenpox). Associated with Pitta-Rakta vitiation causing skin eruptions.

Group of 20 urinary anomaly syndromes characterised by increased frequency, turbidity and altered characteristics of urine. Classified into Kaphaja (10 types), Pittaja (6 types) and Vataja (4 types). Broadly correlates with diabetes mellitus and other metabolic urinary conditions.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Group of urinary anomaly syndromes with increased frequency and turbidity of urine

diseases.description: Metabolic disorder characterised by elevated blood glucose from insufficient insulin production or action. The most important sub-type of Prameha; Madhumeha corresponds to diabetes mellitus. Features sweet, honey-like urine.
Protrusion of rectal tissue through the anal opening; may be partial or complete. Often associated with chronic constipation, diarrhoea or weakness of pelvic floor muscles.

Ayurvedic anti-ageing and rejuvenation therapy promoting longevity, immunity, cognitive function, strength and vitality. One of the eight branches of Ayurveda (Ashtanga). Nourishes all seven Dhatus and protects Ojas.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting body strength; muscular strength; resistance to diseases; tonic

diseases.description: Specific group of Rasayana herbs that directly promote Medha (intellect), memory, cognitive function and learning ability. The four classical Medhya Rasayana herbs are Mandukaparni, Yastimadhu, Guduchi and Shankhapushpi — with Brahmi and Jyotismati also highly prominent.
Inability to voluntarily pass urine; acute or chronic urinary retention from obstruction, neurological causes or prostate enlargement.
Fungal skin infection (dermatophytosis / tinea) causing ring-shaped, scaly, itchy patches on skin, scalp or nails.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Ringworm; scaly and exudative affections of the skin

diseases.description: Abnormal enlargement of the scrotum; may indicate hydrocele, haematocele, inguinal hernia, orchitis or lymphatic obstruction.
General category of skin diseases including eczema, dermatitis, psoriasis and other cutaneous disorders not classified under Kushtha.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Abnormal enlargement of the spleen; may indicate infection, haematological disorder, portal hypertension or liver disease.
Heat illness from prolonged exposure to high temperature or direct sun; body temperature regulation failure causing confusion, high fever and collapse.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A type of headache beginning with sunrise and increasing with the sun's movements

diseases.description: Sexually transmitted bacterial infection (Treponema pallidum) progressing through primary (chancre), secondary (rash) and tertiary stages with multi-organ involvement.
Excessive or pathological thirst; persistent desire to drink beyond normal hydration needs. May indicate dehydration, fever, diabetes or Pitta aggravation.
Group of eight abdominal disorders (Ashtavidha Udara Roga) including ascites, enlargement from various Doshic causes. Jalodara (ascites) is the most serious form.

Allergic skin reaction causing raised, itchy, reddish welts (wheals) of systemic origin; triggered by allergens, cold, heat or stress. Sitapitta — cold and Pitta combination — is the Ayurvedic equivalent.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Urticaria; an allergic disease with rashes, redness, painful and itching skin elevations
Sitapitta / Kotha-Udarda; allied to urticaria; severe skin patches
Anti-pruritic; indicated in scabies, itchy troubles and similar complaints

diseases.description: Paralysis or stiffness of lower limbs; may be neurological (from spinal cord or nerve involvement) or from excessive Kapha and Meda accumulation obstructing Vata channels.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Painful joint inflammation caused by uric acid crystal deposition; primarily affects the big toe and lower limb joints. Caused by vitiation of both Vata and Rakta (blood) doshas in Ayurveda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disease caused by vitiation of Vata and Rakta; gout
Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis

diseases.description: Broad group of 80 diseases caused by aggravated Vata dosha; includes paralysis, pain syndromes, convulsions, tremors, motor disorders, sensory deficits and neurodegenerative conditions.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system
A principal component of Tridosha; generally known as wind or gas

diseases.description: Pain radiating along the sciatic nerve from lower back through hip and down the leg; often with numbness and weakness. The characteristic gait resembles the vulture (Gridhra) — hence the name.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Chronic inflammatory arthritis with persistent joint pain, swelling and progressive degeneration; joint deformity in advanced stages.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata

diseases.description: Inability to open the mouth due to sustained spasm of jaw muscles; classically associated with tetanus (Dhanustambha) or severe Vata vitiation in the jaw region.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Sexually transmitted disease causing painful genital ulcers (soft chancre / chancroid); distinct from syphilitic hard chancre. Caused by bacteria with ulceration and inguinal lymphadenopathy.
Inflammation of stomach and intestines causing vomiting, diarrhoea, piercing abdominal pain and cramps. Visuchika is a severe acute form corresponding to cholera-like gastroenteritis.

Chronic skin condition causing loss of melanin pigmentation in patches; white or depigmented patches on skin. Caused by destruction of melanocytes. Svitra in Ayurveda is classified as a Kushtha variant.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Useful in promoting complexion of the skin (pigmentation)
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Forceful expulsion of stomach contents through the mouth. Classified as Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Dvandvaja and Sannipataja in Ayurveda. Includes morning sickness and post-toxin vomiting.
Progressive loss of body weight, muscle mass and strength; general debility and emaciation from depleted Dhatus, chronic disease or inadequate nutrition.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting body strength; muscular strength; tonic

diseases.description: Infestation with intestinal parasitic worms including roundworms (Ascaris), tapeworms, hookworms and threadworms. Krmi in Ayurveda also includes microorganisms causing disease.
Parasitic infection by Dracunculus medinensis (guinea worm); a long worm that slowly emerges through the skin causing intense burning pain.
Chronic autoimmune skin condition causing accelerated skin cell turnover; rounded reddened patches covered with dry silvery scales. Recurrent and relapsing.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Psoriasis; chronic skin inflammation with rounded reddened silvery-scaled patches
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Dark spots or hyperpigmented patches on the face caused by stress and excessive exercise; melasma-like condition. In Ayurveda, a minor Kushtha type from aggravated Vata and Pitta.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Dark shade on face caused by stress and excessive exercise
Useful in promoting complexion of the skin (pigmentation)
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Premature or progressive greying of hair from loss of melanin in hair follicles; may be related to Pitta aggravation, nutritional deficiency or genetic factors.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Restoration of skin pigmentation in depigmented or leucodermic areas; photosensitising herbs used to stimulate melanocyte activity in vitiligo management.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Useful in promoting complexion of the skin (pigmentation)
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Presence of blood in urine (haematuria); may indicate kidney disease, bladder infection, urinary stones or urological malignancy. Raktameha is one of the Pittaja Prameha types.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Dysuria associated with burning sensation and haematuria
